g.text: You paste rough requirements. Three experts work one after another. You get a finished prompt. Nobody asks you anything.
one run of the skill (the session that runs it only moves files between the experts)
settles the goal, who it is for,
the role the work calls for,
in that field: every task defined,
has not seen the experts' reasoning;
gaps found: sent back, then a fresh checker checks again (at most 3 checks)
the checker reads only your original message and the prompt
the requirements expert also reads your own words, not a summary
Three rules that hold for every run
Where your message is ambiguous the
experts choose as an expert would,
and tell you what they chose.
Every requirement you wrote can be
pointed to in the prompt. It may be
The prompt says what is wanted and
what done looks like. It names no
Sources with their dates, findings with quotes,
and what they settled. The experts apply it, so a
run needs no web access. It settled two choices:
- the prompt does not open with an expert role
- the experts are subagents, not teammates
Say "redo the research" to refresh it.
Illustrations from the public Excalidraw libraries: Robots, Stick Figures, IT icons, Checkmarks.
